title: Review: entire MIME workspace
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — One panic-instead-of-Err in encrypt() (RNG failure), one guidance comment that leads P-521 users into a broken sign/verify combination, and one test suite that panics rather than skips when openssl is absent. No memory unsafety, no data corruption. The correctness surface is well-tested for the RSA+AES path; risk is primarily in edge cases (P-521, non-conformant CA chains, adversarial content).
Confidence: 15% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: (1) RFC 5652 §5.4 signed attribute DER encoding (IMPLICIT [0] vs EXPLICIT SET) — the sign/verify round-trip test passes but I did not independently verify the DER encoding byte-by-byte; (2) chain_depth semantics in cert.rs pathLen check — logic appears correct but was reasoned about rather than tested with a 3-deep chain. Would raise confidence if: round-trip test with a P-384 ECDH encrypted message was present; integration test against a real-world S/MIME email with a 3-level chain was present.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — Code is generally idiomatic Rust. No unsafe, no gratuitous clones, error types are non_exhaustive, public API uses owned types. Main issues: (1) pre-1.0 string-wrapped error variants that will fossilize before v1.0; (2) reference-layer accumulation in cert.rs that confuses type reasoning; (3) minor allocation patterns in non-hot paths.
Rust idiom confidence: 10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: DER-encoding path for SignedAttributes (correct behavior verified by round-trip test but not byte-checked independently). Uncertainty driven by: the cms/der crate API surface is pre-release (=0.3.0-pre.2) and its encoding behavior is not fully specified in public docs.
